title: Ulyana and the Oath
premise: Edmund Galloway, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead, has spent years hiding his gift while guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains. When the crown declares a hunt for all gifted souls, he flees with Ulyana, a disgraced royal oath-keeper whose broken covenant between the human realm and the spirit realm caused the dead to fall silent and the mountains to sour. Hunted by Inquisitor Vael and tempted by a spirit lord offering power in exchange for Ulyana's surrender, they must reforge the ancient covenant before the thirteenth moon turns. In the end, Edmund binds his own voice to the covenant, giving up hearing the dead forever, while Ulyana chooses love over her reclaimed duty — sealing the realms together at the cost of everything each once was.
about_author: Orsen Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former stonemason from the northern valleys who claims to have learned storytelling from graveyard caretakers and mountain mail-carriers. They write slow-burning fantasy about ordinary hands holding extraordinary burdens, and refuse to appear in public without gloves.

chapters.title: The Bone-Carver's Silence
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In his workshop above Thornfell village, Edmund carves a memorial whistle for a drowned child and hears the dead whisper warnings: the crown is coming. A royal proclamation names the gifted as traitors. Emotional beat: dread settling over a man who has hidden his true self his whole life.

chapters.title: The Oath-Keeper's Fall
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Disgraced and exiled to a border garrison, Ulyana remembers the night she refused to renew the covenant and let the spirit realm go dark. Now she learns the silence in the mountains is spreading — and that the crown blames people like Edmund, not her failure. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Pass
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Inquisitor Vael burns the village shrine and interrogates the smugglers Edmund guides. Edmund flees into the high passes and collides with Ulyana, also running, carrying the shattered Oathstone. Uneasy alliance forms. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's masks.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The dead guide Edmund through a forgotten covenant-road only spirits remember, forcing him to reveal his gift to Ulyana. She confesses she broke the covenant deliberately, believing both realms better off unbound. Emotional beat: intimacy born of confession, shadowed by betrayal.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the ruined Covenant Hall, they learn the ritual requires an oath freely given by one of royal blood — but Vael's riders close in, and a spirit lord named Ashvael offers Edmund the power to end the hunt if he delivers Ulyana. Emotional beat: temptation pressing on loyalty.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Hunt
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Captured by Vael, Edmund bargains with half-truths while Ulyana stages a rescue using smuggler tricks and the dead's whispered intelligence. Vael reveals the crown wants the covenant reforged too — under its own terms, with a puppet oath-keeper. Emotional beat: fury at being pawns.

chapters.title: The Price of a Voice
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Hidden in the deep caves, Ulyana discovers the original covenant was sealed by a bone-carver who gave up hearing the dead — the ritual's true cost. She realizes what Edmund will try and begs him not to. Emotional beat: love confronting sacrifice, first spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Hollow Gate
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Ashvael captures Ulyana, revealing it engineered the crown's hunt to force a flawed renewal it could control. Edmund pretends to accept the bargain, walking Ulyana to the gate as bait. Emotional beat: cold clarity — a man weaponizing his own grief.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the Covenant Hall under the thirteenth full moon, Edmund speaks the old words and offers his voice; Ulyana refuses the throne's pardon and gives her oath freely instead. Ashvael unravels as the true covenant takes hold. Climax: both realms answer together, and the dead sing one last time.

chapters.title: A Quiet Hand
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, epilogue-like. The silence Edmund chose holds — he carves bones now only for beauty, guided by memory rather than ghosts. Ulyana, stripped of rank, stays in Thornfell as its record-keeper. They rebuild the village shrine side by side. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity remade, love chosen daily.
